shape: lib/ncd/catalog/schema.ts (briefing Appendix A). Keys named 'x' are outside the schema: provenance, lane and family, and proposed fields.

x.note: The briefing showed only 'known'. 'not_known' is proposed so that a rule can tell 'recorded as not diabetic' from 'not recorded' (F15). Phase 0 maps both to the live options.

Entry must offer mmol/L and mg/dL and convert in the platform, never in the clinician's head: a mg/dL value typed into a mmol/L box satisfies every threshold (F25). The plausibility range is a platform parameter for CSO signature; the pack types no number for it.

The live options have no 'confused'. A confused, hyperglycaemic patient is not caught by the rules that read drowsiness: Phase 0 adds the option, or maps the clerking desk's confusion finding to it, and the acute rules read it (second review, H41).

citation.quote: ASCVD broadly refers to a history of acute coronary syndrome, myocardial infarction (MI), stable or unstable angina or coronary or other arterial revascularization, stroke, or peripheral artery disease (PAD) including aortic aneurysm and is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in people with diabetes.

features.display: Meter shows HI or LO instead of a number

x.note: The two most dangerous readings are not numbers. HI satisfies the acute rules, the suspicion rule, the same-day referral and the symptomatic criterion; LO satisfies the hypoglycaemia rule. No number is invented for either.

features.display: Could be pregnant (computed by the platform from sex and age)

x.note: When this is true and 'pregnant' is not recorded, every rule that applies only outside pregnancy is 'insufficient: pregnancy status needed' (F09). The platform owns the age band.
